papers.title: CD97/ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma.
papers.summary: CD97 loss exacerbates type 2 allergic asthma in female mice; CD97 antibody before sensitization worsens responses. CD97-/- mice show more conventional type 2 and monocyte-derived dendritic cells; allergen-pulsed CD97-/- BMDCs drive stronger CD4 type 2 cytokine secretion and airway inflammation. ADGRE5 is reduced in human asthmatic mononuclear phagocytes after exacerbation, identifying CD97 as a regulator and potential asthma target.

papers.title: A New agent in the matrix: PINK1's expanded role in mitochondrial surveillance and Regulation.
papers.summary: Commentary proposing a third fate for PINK1 beyond partial import/cleavage and parkin-dependent mitophagy: matrix entry in active mitochondria. Unusual transmembrane-domain properties confer a conformational switch, suggesting an additional mitophagy-independent regulatory role inside the matrix, expanding PINK1 biology beyond quality-control surveillance.

papers.title: A transient RNP compartment boosts translation and growth of mammalian oocytes.
papers.summary: Growing mouse oocytes harbor a transient ribonucleoprotein compartment named the zollo body, identified by immunofluorescence, mass spectrometry, electron microscopy, RNA-seq and live ovarian-slice imaging. It resembles the Balbiani body but arises during growth and shows nascent translation and phospho-mTOR enrichment. Pharmacological dissolution arrests follicle and oocyte growth, indicating a required translation-associated compartment.

papers.title: Sorting of lysosomal enzyme and autophagy are regulated by the GGA1-induced TGN lipid scrambling.
papers.summary: GGA1 exposes sphingomyelin on the cytoplasmic surface of the trans-Golgi network via its GAT domain, dependent on membrane curvature and cholesterol. This exposure coincides with mannose 6-phosphate receptor exit required for lysosomal enzyme trafficking, and sphingomyelin transfers to autophagic membranes facilitating autophagosome-lysosome fusion, revealing a role for lipid remodeling in membrane trafficking and autophagy.

papers.title: SpotMAX: A generalist framework for multidimensional automatic spot detection and quantification.
papers.summary: SpotMAX is a generalist AI-assisted framework for automated spot detection and quantification in 3D data, with a GUI and cell segmentation/tracking. It outperforms or matches state-of-the-art tools and human annotators on a large 3D dataset, applied to C. elegans meiotic crossovers, yeast mitochondrial DNA dynamics, and mouse stem cell telomere length, yielding new biological insights.

papers.title: The structure of the dopamine D(3) receptor bound to cariprazine reveals principles for partial agonists with designed pharmacology.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of the dopamine D3 receptor bound to cariprazine and derivatives (inverse to high-efficacy partial agonists) reveal how chemical modifications map to functional outcomes. Partial agonism reflects small ligand positional shifts within the orthosteric site; the extended site modulates stability, affinity and selectivity. Designed derivatives show enhanced D3/D2 selectivity, providing a structural blueprint for tailored D3R ligands.

papers.title: LATS1/2 inactivation drives a distinct venous endothelial cell response that contributes to fibrotic remodeling of the lung.
papers.summary: Endothelial inactivation of LATS1/2 elicits distinct responses by vascular bed: a reactive injury-like state in capillary endothelium and a separate profibrotic state in a venous population marked by EBF1 and ACKR1. This venous expansion associates with fibroblast activation, macrophage accumulation and epithelial remodeling. Pharmacologic YAP/TAZ-TEAD inhibition prevents fibrotic remodeling, identifying LATS1/2 restraint of YAP/TAZ as essential for lung endothelial homeostasis.

papers.title: SHARPIN restrains IL-33 release by stromal cells to control ILC2 inflammation.
papers.summary: Sharpin deficiency increases type 2 innate lymphoid cells in lung and other tissues through enhanced IL-33 production by lung stromal cells. Sharpin directly binds IL-33 via its pleckstrin homology-linker region and restrains its release independently of ubiquitination. Combined Sharpin and IL-33 deficiency reverses ILC2 increase and lung inflammation, revealing a non-canonical, ubiquitin-independent gatekeeper function of Sharpin.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structures of Cdr1 reveal snapshots of substrate transport and diverse inhibitor recognition.
papers.summary: Seven cryo-EM structures of the Candida albicans ABC transporter Cdr1 capture substrate entry and expulsion during multidrug resistance. An inward-facing channel with three on-off substrate binding sites defines an entry pathway; ATP binding closes the transmembrane domain to expel substrate, and ADP release resets the transporter. Three diverse inhibitors reveal two binding modes, providing structural blueprints for antifungal drug design.

papers.title: Programmable protein degraders enable selective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin subpopulations in vitro and in vivo.
papers.summary: Designer ubiquibodies (UABs) combining an E3 ligase with computationally designed guide peptides selectively degrade pathogenic cytosolic and nuclear β-catenin while preserving the membrane-associated pool. This suppresses Wnt/β-catenin signaling and impairs colorectal cancer cell survival and proliferation. An LNP-encapsulated mRNA delivery selectively reduced cytosolic β-catenin in mouse livers, demonstrating peptide-programmable degraders active in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Structure-function analysis of the FCRL5-IgG1 Fc complex reveals an unappreciated pathway for B cell modulation by Fc-attenuated IgG.
papers.summary: Crystal structure of the FCRL5-IgG1 Fc complex (3.4 Å) reveals a 1:1 binding mode distinct from classical Fcγ receptors, explaining why Fc-effector-silencing mutations spare FCRL5 binding. Fc-attenuated therapeutic IgG retains FCRL5 engagement, and FCRL5-selective antibodies inhibited BCR-induced Ca2+ flux in FCRL5-expressing B cells, identifying an unappreciated pathway for B cell modulation.

papers.title: Neuron-derived SPP1 instructs microglia to limit degeneration.
papers.summary: Neuron-derived SPP1 (secreted phosphoprotein 1) reprograms microglia to a neuroprotective, homeostatic state after injury and during neurodegeneration. In glaucoma and optic nerve damage models, SPP1 enhances microglial autophagy, debris clearance and anti-inflammatory activity, preserving neuronal survival and visual function. SPP1 is elevated in human/primate glaucomatous retinas and correlates with neuronal survival in Alzheimer's disease, defining a protective neuron-microglia axis.

papers.title: Hi-Cformer enables multiscale chromatin contact map modeling for single-cell Hi-C data analysis.
papers.summary: Hi-Cformer is a transformer method that simultaneously models multiscale blocks of sparse single-cell Hi-C contact maps via a specialized attention mechanism. It learns robust low-dimensional cell representations, improving cell type separation versus existing methods, accurately imputes interaction signals including TAD-like boundaries and A/B compartments, and enables accurate cell type annotation across intra- and inter-dataset scenarios.

papers.title: Tracking breast cancer progression using Methylscape.
papers.summary: The Methylscape, a cancer DNA methylation landscape of promoter hypermethylation and gene body hypomethylation, can monitor cancer progression. In a TGF-β-induced breast cancer EMT model, mesenchymal DNA showed increased Methylscape enrichment, sensitively detecting epigenetic remodeling. A gold-based DNA desorption platform and a low-cost screen-printed electrode enable stage-specific breast cancer monitoring, supporting non-invasive clinical translation.

papers.title: Maladaptive immune-fibrotic axis drives impaired long bone regeneration under mechanical instability.
papers.summary: A murine delayed-fracture model using tunable intramedullary fixation imposed controlled interfragmentary strain. High-strain calluses showed delayed ossification, 3.3-fold more fibrotic tissue and reduced biomechanical integrity. Spatial transcriptomics identified persistent fibrotic niches (PDGFRB, LGALS3) and dysregulated macrophage-fibroblast signaling (SPP1, MMP9); early immune polarization (CD206+ macrophages, CD25+ Tregs) predicted healing. Establishes a preclinical platform for mechanobiology-informed fracture therapies.

papers.title: Progressive oxygenation of developing leaves directs morphogenesis.
papers.summary: Developing leaves form a spatiotemporal oxygen gradient sensed via the plant cysteine oxidase N-degron pathway. Early hypoxia restricts cell expansion, while subsequent distal-to-proximal oxygenation depletes group VII ethylene response factors, enabling specialized cell-fate acquisition and controlling proliferation. Oxygen acts as a positional cue guiding leaf morphogenesis, suggesting opportunities to harness oxygen gradients to direct plant form and function.

papers.title: A spatially resolved implantable microdevice for multiplexed in situ screening of engineered cellular therapies in solid tumors.
papers.summary: A miniaturized implantable microdevice (iMD) with discrete fibrin-filled reservoirs enables spatially resolved, multiplexed delivery and screening of T cell therapies directly within live tumors. In glioblastoma xenografts, EGFR-targeting CAR-T reservoirs showed dense CD8+ infiltration, cleaved-caspase-3 apoptosis and suppressed Ki67 versus minimal activity in controls. The platform facilitates parallel in vivo evaluation of immune cell therapies for solid tumors.

papers.title: Ninjurin-1 mediates hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.summary: Ninjurin-1 (NINJ1) aggregates in the plasma membrane to permeabilize cells during lytic cell death driving hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI). NINJ1 genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition diminished acute injury in mice and rats; hepatocyte- or macrophage-specific knockout reduced injury. NINJ1 is positioned as a potential therapeutic target to limit hepatic IRI, with implications for liver transplantation.

papers.title: IDE-mediated GLP-1 degradation as the basis for designing long-acting and CNS-stable GLP-1 receptor agonists.
papers.summary: Insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE) is identified as a previously unknown GLP-1-degrading protease with two cleavage sites, regulating glucose control. Engineered GLP-1 and semaglutide with D-amino acid substitutions at these sites resist degradation and show enhanced stability in plasma, tissues, and CNS. D-Ser18-semaglutide shows prolonged plasma retention and sustained glucose lowering in mice, informing long-acting agonist design.

papers.title: Metabolic control of smooth muscle cell phenotype switching in atherosclerosis.
papers.summary: TGFβ induces ACSS2-dependent acetyl-CoA by suppressing PDK4, stabilizing R-Smads and TGFβ receptor 1 to preserve smooth muscle cell contractile phenotype. Smooth-muscle-specific PDK4 knockout increased glucose-derived acetyl-CoA and contractile phenotype, reducing atherosclerosis in ApoE knockout mice. Human specimens show a strong correlation between PDK4 level and atherosclerosis severity, linking carbohydrate metabolism to SMC phenotype maintenance.

papers.title: Muscular dystrophy-associated lamin variants disrupt cellular organization through a nucleolar-ribosomal axis.
papers.summary: In C. elegans Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy models, disease-linked lamin variants reduce cytoplasmic mesoscale crowding, increase molecular diffusivity, and disrupt nuclear positioning and ER architecture, mirroring ribosome depletion. Lamin dysfunction lowers nucleolar fibrillarin and ribosome abundance, revealing a nucleolar-ribosomal axis transmitting nuclear defects to the cytoplasm. LEM-domain protein loss phenocopies the mutants, connecting nuclear architecture to whole-cell biophysics.

papers.title: Insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 7 is a soluble cell adhesion molecule.
papers.summary: IGFBP7 assembles into a barrel-shaped dodecamer in the presence of heparin, resolved by cryo-EM: the C-terminal IgC2 domain forms the core, capped by N-terminal heparin-binding domains. The homo-oligomer simultaneously engages heparan sulfate proteoglycans on adjacent cells, functioning as a soluble cell adhesion molecule that enhances and prolongs receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, establishing it as a universal adhesion factor.

papers.title: The molecular basis of mitochondrial crista formation by the MIC10 complex.
papers.summary: The MIC10 subcomplex proteins (MIC10, MIC26, MIC27) recruit cardiolipin at conserved positive loop motifs, driving oligomerization and stabilizing membrane curvature, shown by structure prediction and multiscale simulations. Reconstructing the full MIC10 complex in a crista junction setup shows it maintains membrane bending, with disordered regions possibly forming a permeability barrier, providing a mechanistic model for cristae curvature.

papers.title: An axon-intrinsic loop restricts nerve regeneration through axonal protein synthesis.
papers.summary: Injured axons synthesize the RNA-binding protein KHSRP, which promotes mRNA decay and slows nerve regeneration. Axotomy-induced axoplasmic Ca2+ activates KHSRP translation; a Reg3a-dependent loop sustains it via ER Ca2+ release, PERK and eIF2α phosphorylation. Reg3a depletion attenuates growth-cone Ca2+ oscillations, decreases KHSRP synthesis, reduces axonal retractive events, and accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration in vivo.

papers.title: Bacteriophage PAK_P3 genome structuration and dynamics during infection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal specific interaction patterns.
papers.summary: This study maps 3D genome folding of the virulent double-stranded DNA phage PAK_P3 during Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection. The phage genome rapidly decondenses into a specific organization reflecting its transcriptional program, while the host genome decondenses as gene expression wanes. Specific phage-host chromosome contacts are uncovered, showing the phage exploits host spatial genome architecture during its infection cycle.

papers.title: Activation of G(12)-type G proteins in pancreatic β cells protects against impaired glucose homeostasis.
papers.summary: Selective activation of β-cell G12-type G protein signaling strongly promoted insulin secretion, protecting mice against obesity-associated metabolic deficits and improving glycemic control in a type 2 diabetes model. Mechanistic studies in perfused islets identified ROCK as a key downstream effector triggering insulin secretion. GPCRs linked to G12 in β cells are proposed as potential antidiabetic drug targets.

papers.title: Carbon ion irradiation at a clinically used dose rewires super-enhancers to drive necroptosis and systemic immunity.
papers.summary: A physical dose of 2 Gy of carbon ions provokes antitumor immunity in a high-LET-specific, dose-independent manner. Carbon ions rewire death to MLKL-dependent necroptosis and drive an NF-κB inflammatory cascade, surpassing 8 Gy x-rays in immunogenicity. Clustered DNA damage drives super-enhancer remodeling suppressing apoptosis while licensing necroptosis. In vivo, 2 Gy carbon ion therapy drives abscopal responses, informing radio-immunotherapy integration.

papers.title: Cardiac tertiary immune niches drive immune activation in immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis.
papers.summary: Using integrated spatial and single-cell analyses in a pharmacological model of immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis, regional Ly6C+ monocyte and PD-1+ CD8+ T cell infiltration organized into fibroblast-rich tertiary T cell niches. A niche gene signature was enriched in patient cardiac tissue, with clonal T cell expansion. Niche-associated cytokines and structural proteins are candidate targets to reduce ICI cardiotoxicity.

papers.title: Algae-specific immune modulation influences responses to heat and pathogen challenge in a symbiotic coral.
papers.summary: In the coral Pocillopora acuta, hosting Durusdinium algae confers thermotolerance but predisposes to stress-related tissue loss, with higher immune-related gene expression and baseline NF-κB. Under heat, D-hosting corals showed tissue loss, oxidative stress and immune dysregulation, while Cladocopium-hosting corals were more bleaching-susceptible. Vibrio infection caused high tissue loss only in D-hosting corals, revealing immune trade-offs from symbiont association.

papers.title: Loss of the mitochondrial SAM transporter reveals a lipoylation-dependent metabolic vulnerability in the postnatal heart.
papers.summary: Mitochondrial S-adenosylmethionine import through SLC25A26 becomes limiting shortly after birth and specifically restricts protein lipoylation during postnatal heart metabolic growth. Loss of SLC25A26 impairs pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase flux, depleting aspartate and nucleotide pools, with sustained cardiomyocyte cycling, delayed maturation and early cardiomyopathy. Medium-chain triglyceride supplementation stabilized metabolism and prolonged survival, identifying a stage-specific metabolic vulnerability.

papers.title: Truthful visualizations for mass spectrometry imaging enable high-spatial-resolution interactive m/z mapping and exploration.
papers.summary: MSI-Visual is an open-source framework for interactive mass spectrometry imaging analysis integrating truthful dimensionality-reduction visualizations, region-of-interest selection, statistical comparison, and direct m/z mapping. It introduces four visualization strategies optimized for global structure preservation or memory-efficient rapid visualization. On benchmarks and lipidomics case studies it outperforms alternatives, detecting subtle tissue differences and fine molecular-anatomical patterns for discovery and diagnostic workflows.

papers.title: Multiheme selenoenzyme essential for elemental sulfur respiration.
papers.summary: A conserved multiheme cytochrome c selenoprotein is identified as essential for elemental sulfur reduction in a sulfur-respiring bacterium. The enzyme forms a tetramer, each subunit containing five hemes and one selenocysteine, catalyzing polysulfide reduction at an active site where cysteine coordinates heme iron and selenocysteine is essential for catalysis. Both residues are critical for sulfur respiration in vivo, expanding understanding of microbial energy metabolism.

papers.title: RIBOTAC-mediated degradation of hsa-microRNA-301a-3p suppresses TNBC bone metastasis.
papers.summary: Integrative bioinformatics and machine learning identified hsa-miR-301a-3p as a central regulator of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) bone metastasis. A designed RIBOTAC recruits endogenous RNase L to degrade the primary pri-miRNA, reducing miR-301a-3p, restoring NEDD4L, promoting YAP degradation, and suppressing TNBC bone metastasis, demonstrating RNA-targeted degradation as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Transposable Elements and the Impact of Genomic Autoimmunity.
papers.summary: This Annual Review of Genetics article discusses how transposable element (TE) replication is limited by Argonaute proteins guided by small RNAs detecting TE transcripts, in maize and Drosophila. Because genomic immunity is imperfect, off-target small RNA silencing can silence real genes. This shapes TE evolutionary dynamics, establishes novel modes of adaptation and epigenetic inheritance, and generates feedback that shapes gene silencing evolution.

papers.title: Budding yeast Bud3 and Bud4 cooperatively organize septin architecture and support cytokinetic spatial memory.
papers.summary: Bud3 and Bud4 organize septin filaments in distinct ways and cooperate to assemble complex higher-order networks during budding yeast cytokinesis. They bind different septins and possess lipid-binding domains involved in bud-neck recruitment and septin organization. In bud3 bud4 double mutants, the double ring is essential for concentrating proteins marking cytokinetic remnants, acting as a selective spatial memory of cytokinesis.

papers.title: SANS ankyrin repeats mediate non-classical nuclear import and dictate distinct pathogenic mechanisms.
papers.summary: High-resolution crystal structures of the N-terminal ankyrin repeat (AR) regions of SANS and its homolog ANKS4B show SANS_AR is a self-sufficient nuclear localization module, while ANKS4B_AR is not. Structure-guided analysis of Usher 1G variants reveals two classes: core hydrophobic mutations (L48P, L84P) destabilize the domain, whereas surface substitutions (R10W, S119P, R146C) reduce nuclear localization, informing USH1G pathogenesis.

papers.title: HDAC1/2-mediated repression of Wnt receptor expression orients asymmetric division polarity in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: Class I histone deacetylase hda-1 (homologous to HDAC1/2) controls polarity orientation during asymmetric division of C. elegans epidermal seam stem cells. Tissue-specific loss causes polarity reversals and reduced molecular asymmetry, with upregulation of Wnt receptors lin-17 (Frizzled) and cam-1 (ROR). Overexpression of either receptor reproduces the reversals. Graded, opposing receptor expression along the body axis may orient division polarity.

papers.title: Engineered outer membrane vesicle-like nanoparticles from Lactobacillus plantarum for oral IL-22 mRNA delivery and treatment of DSS-induced colitis.
papers.summary: Engineered Lactobacillus plantarum-derived outer-membrane-vesicle-like nanoparticles delivered oral IL-22 mRNA (72.43% encapsulation) that was protected from RNase and stable under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. The formulation was taken up by intestinal epithelial cells, increased IL-22 and STAT3 activation, and enhanced barrier proteins and transepithelial resistance. In DSS-induced colitis it mitigated weight loss, disease scores and inflammation while restoring epithelial barrier.

papers.title: Celastrol alleviates synovial inflammation and joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis in association with Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 pathway activation.
papers.summary: Celastrol reduced paw swelling, arthritis scores and serum IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α in collagen-induced arthritis rats while attenuating synovial hyperplasia, cartilage damage and osteoclast activation. It increased Nrf2, HO-1 and GPX4 expression and reduced ROS and Fe2+ accumulation. In TNF-α-stimulated fibroblast-like synoviocytes, celastrol suppressed proliferation, migration and invasion and increased apoptosis, effects enhanced by TBHQ and attenuated by brusatol.

papers.title: Small extracellular vesicles induced by Angiotensin-(1-7) enhance cardioprotection following myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.summary: Ang-(1-7) stimulated cardiomyocytes to release small extracellular vesicles (sEV) with enhanced cardioprotective effects, largely Mas receptor-independent. In myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury models, sEV preserved cardiac function by attenuating cardiomyocyte apoptosis and oxidative stress, even with Mas inhibition or knockout, and outperformed direct Ang-(1-7). Vesicles increased AKT2 phosphorylation and SERCA activity while suppressing ER stress; AKT2 knockdown weakened the benefits.

papers.title: Lactic acid exposure alters lysophosphatidic acid receptor-mediated regulation of growth and motility in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.summary: Long-term lactic acid exposure (1 or 5 mM) generated PANC-LA1 and PANC-LA5 pancreatic cancer cells with elevated LPAR1/3/5 and reduced LPAR2 expression. LPA inhibited PANC-1 growth but enhanced LA1/LA5 motility; pharmacological probes (AM966, TC LPA5 4, GRI-977,143, (2S)-OMPT) confirmed LPAR1 and LPAR3 as major positive regulators of proliferation and motility after lactic acid exposure, with LPAR2 and LPAR5 playing distinct roles.

papers.title: Liensinine-loaded extracellular vesicles mitigate osteoporosis through inhibition of NF-κB signaling and calcium oscillations in osteoclasts.
papers.summary: Endothelial-cell-derived extracellular vesicles loaded with liensinine (Lie@EVs) enhanced delivery to osteoclasts and inhibited osteoclast differentiation and bone resorption compared with free liensinine. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified NF-κB and calcium signaling as targets. Mechanistically, Lie@EVs suppressed NF-κB pathway activation and calcium oscillations, downregulating osteoclast-specific gene expression, supporting potential for osteoporosis treatment.

papers.title: Mixed evidence that dosage sensitive genes drive global dosage compensation in flour beetles.
papers.summary: Testing the insensitive sex chromosome hypothesis across five flour beetle species, including a neo-X from an X-autosome fusion, comparative transcriptomics showed complete chromosome-wide dosage compensation and balance in somatic tissues, including the neo-X. Neither ancestral nor neo-X is depleted of RNAi-sensitive genes, but at the gene level there is little evidence sensitive genes show reduced expression divergence, suggesting global regulatory compensation persists through sex chromosome turnover.

papers.title: Understanding genomic landscapes of differentiation in round-tailed horned lizards (Phrynosoma modestum).
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of round-tailed horned lizards supports two lineages with a north/south divide around 7 Ma and little migration, though intermediate genealogical divergence indexes preclude a full taxonomic distinction. Genomic scans identified islands of divergence; significantly negative Tajima's D and positive selection statistics suggest selection (possibly from recent population expansion) shaped divergence, with within-population selection playing a large role.

papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing revealed local genetic differences and multi-layered genetic structure in Asian brown bear (Ursus arctos) populations.
papers.summary: Whole-genome resequencing of Asian brown bears revealed a multi-layered genetic structure from multiple demographic events. Autosomal divergence times in central/west Asian populations differed by hundreds of thousands of years from mitochondrial/Y-chromosomal estimates, suggesting continued gene flow after dispersal. Y-phylogeny and f4 statistics indicated differentiation between Kazakhstan and Tibetan populations likely from male-biased introgression; Hokkaido and Etorofu populations retained polar-bear-derived alleles.

papers.title: NECTIN2 depletion impairs migration and invasion in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells through LIMK1-associated cytoskeletal remodeling.
papers.summary: NECTIN2 expression is elevated in breast cancer and associated with poorer recurrence-free survival in triple-negative patients. Silencing NECTIN2 reduced migration and invasion in MDA-MB-231 (but not MDA-MB-468) cells, with reduced LIMK1 expression. Ectopic LIMK1 partially restored migration with partial EMT-like changes (decreased E-cadherin/ZO-1, increased fibronectin and Snail), suggesting NECTIN2 drives invasive phenotypes via LIMK1-associated cytoskeletal remodeling.

papers.title: Combining a diffusion model with a sparse coding strategy to improve the machine translation accuracy of culturally loaded words in English news texts.
papers.summary: This paper combines a diffusion model with sparse coding to translate culturally loaded words in English news. A sparse semantic extraction module strengthens key cultural information, and a diffusion generation mechanism reconstructs the target text through denoising with time-step-aware gating and cultural ontology constraints. It achieves higher BLEU-4 and METEOR scores on long-tail news and improved accuracy/recall on unregistered vocabulary.

papers.title: Exploration of acetylation-related biomarkers in osteoarthritis through bioinformatics analysis.
papers.summary: Bioinformatics analysis of osteoarthritis (OA) GEO datasets with WGCNA identified acetylation-related differentially expressed genes; machine learning selected JUN and MYC as biomarkers, validated by qRT-PCR and western blot. A diagnostic prediction model showed strong efficacy (AUC 0.983 training, 0.743 validation) with altered immune cell infiltration. JUN and MYC are proposed as novel acetylation-related biomarkers in OA.

papers.title: Phycocyanobilin: A potential bioactive compound from Arthrospira platensis targeting LYN protein associated with systemic lupus erythematosus.
papers.summary: Phycocyanobilin from Arthrospira platensis, structurally similar to bilirubin, was investigated for systemic lupus erythematosus. Molecular docking showed favorable binding to EGFR, FYN, HLA-B, LCK, LYN and TP53, with LYN as a key target. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable LYN binding comparable to the native ligand staurosporine, suggesting phycocyanobilin may modulate LYN-associated signaling in SLE.

papers.title: Machine Learning approaches for the detection of disease-causing variants in whole-genome data need to address the expression of functional genes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks machine learning approaches for identifying disease-causing variants using real and synthetic datasets with known generating mechanisms. Logistic regression was most reliable at causative gene identification across synthetic datasets despite not always besting classification performance. Training on UK Biobank showed it is necessary to account for the expression of functional genes to successfully predict disease.

papers.title: Cytosolic Fe/S protein biogenesis: a crossroads of Fe/S cluster machineries.
papers.summary: This review provides an updated overview of cytosolic iron-sulfur (Fe/S) protein biogenesis pathways. Genetic evidence across eukaryotes indicates multiple interconnected pathways supply Fe/S clusters to the cytosol and nucleus, with mitochondrial biogenesis providing an exported substrate. Some organisms have replaced the essential mitochondrial system with prokaryotic-derived proteins, which can enable reductive mitochondrial evolution and even complete organelle loss.

papers.title: MicroRNA profiling of filtering and non-filtering regions of human trabecular meshwork: changes with ageing and in glaucoma.
papers.summary: MicroRNA profiling of filtering and non-filtering regions of human trabecular meshwork identified 31 up-regulated and 3 down-regulated miRNAs in the non-filtering region. Validated increases in miR-24-3p, miR-107, miR-34a-5p, miR-184 and decreases in miR-376a-3p, miR-145-5p, miR-22-3p implicate stem cell-related pathways (Wnt, HIF, PI3K-Akt, MAPK). Several showed age-related decline and altered expression in glaucoma, suggesting roles in TMSC regulation.

papers.title: The interplay between chronobiology, neuroinflammation, and the glymphatic system in neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.summary: This conceptual review examines bidirectional crosstalk between the molecular circadian clock, glial-mediated neuroimmunity, and the glymphatic clearance system in neurodegeneration. Loss of circadian temporal gating from aging or sleep fragmentation promotes a vicious cycle: microglial hyperreactivity and disrupted aquaporin-4 polarization impair cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange, accumulating amyloid-β and tau. It highlights chronotherapy, emphasizing melatonin, as a multi-target resynchronizer.

papers.title: Unveiling the role of p53 in the pathogenesis and treatment of autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
papers.summary: This review discusses p53 beyond its tumor-suppressor role in autoimmune rheumatic diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, SLE, systemic sclerosis). Mounting evidence shows p53 regulates immunity, inflammation, angiogenesis, fibrosis, and ferroptosis, maintaining homeostasis and immune tolerance; dysregulation contributes to aberrant immune responses and disease progression. It highlights the potential of p53-based therapies, such as p53 activators, to restore normal activity.

papers.title: Evaluation of phytochemical-mediated inhibition of the efflux pump in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.
papers.summary: This study evaluated efflux pump inhibitory activity of phytochemicals (mirificin, forsythoside A, salvianolic acid A, EGCG, epicatechin gallate) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. All showed dose-dependent biofilm inhibition (>75% reduction at higher concentrations) and enhanced intracellular accumulation of ethidium bromide and Hoechst dye, indicating effective efflux inhibition. Salvianolic acid A (100 µM) showed the highest activity, downregulating mexAB-oprM and quorum-sensing genes.

papers.title: Antitumor properties of fungal-derived compounds: potential applications in skin cancer therapy.
papers.summary: This review summarizes fungal-derived secondary metabolites as anticancer agents for skin cancer, including cordycepin, ganoderic acid D, and polysaccharides like lentinan, acting through pro-apoptotic, anti-angiogenic, immunomodulatory and anti-metastatic mechanisms. It discusses translational challenges (production, bioavailability, toxicity) and potential combinations with chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy. Available data indicate these remain largely preclinical candidates warranting further investigation.

papers.title: Endolysosomal iron-associated vesicular changes and ferroptosis-related vulnerability in VPS13A-knockdown cells.
papers.summary: In VPS13A-knockdown HEK293 cells, oxidant (TBHP) treatment caused elevated lipid peroxidation suppressed by the iron chelator deferasirox or vitamin E. Deferasirox induced enlarged vesicles overlapping Fe(II), lipid peroxidation, lysosomal (Rab7a) and some mitochondrial (Tomm20) signals, consistent with altered iron handling. α-tocopherol reduced oxidative injury without prominent vesicular accumulation, linking lysosome-associated vesicular changes to iron dysregulation in VPS13A disease.

papers.title: Xanthium strumarium L. extract attenuates TNF-α/IFN-γ- stimulated inflammation and promotes hyaluronan production on HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.summary: Xanthium strumarium extract (XSE) showed antioxidant activity without cytotoxicity in HaCaT keratinocytes and attenuated TNF-α/IFN-γ-induced ROS and inflammatory mediators (IL-6, IL-8, TARC, RANTES, CTACK). Mechanistically, it suppressed p38, IκBα and p65 phosphorylation in NF-κB and p38 MAPK signaling, and enhanced hyaluronan production by upregulating hyaluronan synthase transcription. Chlorogenic acid, miquelianin, hyperoside, cynarine and syringetin were major constituents.

papers.title: circBIRC6 regulates cisplatin resistance of choroidal melanoma via positively modulating ERK by sponging miR-503-3p.
papers.summary: circBIRC6 was upregulated in choroidal melanoma tissues and cisplatin-resistant MUM-2B cells. It regulates cisplatin resistance by binding to and sponging miR-503-3p, which directly targets and downregulates ERK1/2. circBIRC6 expression correlated positively with ERK1/2. Knockdown of circBIRC6 may provide an effective treatment strategy for DDP-resistant choroidal melanoma.

papers.title: Integrating non-coding RNA profiling with HPV genotyping for cervical cancer risk stratification and early detection.
papers.summary: This narrative review explores integrating HPV genotyping with non-coding RNA profiling (miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs) as a multi-omics diagnostic approach for cervical cancer risk stratification. ncRNAs are key regulators in HPV-mediated carcinogenesis and are stable in biological fluids, supporting liquid-biopsy use. Combining viral genotype with host molecular responses may improve diagnostic accuracy, though evidence for combined clinical application remains limited and requires prospective validation.

papers.title: Somatic Cells in the Anuran Testis.
papers.journal: Sexual development : genetics, molecular biology, evolution, endocrinology, embryology, and pathology of sex determination and differentiation
papers.summary: This review provides an integrative overview of somatic cells (Sertoli and Leydig cells) in the anuran testis, covering developmental origin, structure and function across primitive and advanced anurans. A distinctive feature is continued Sertoli cell proliferative capacity and cyst formation within adult seminiferous tubules. Although testis differentiation genes are conserved, timing and roles differ in anurans, with gonadal development influenced by steroid hormones.

papers.title: Mitochondria in SARS-CoV-2 infection: Immune interactions and molecular approaches in the Post COVID-19 condition.
papers.summary: This review compiles interactions between SARS-CoV-2 infection and mitochondria, highlighting genetic and immunological mechanisms: increased reactive oxygen species, NLRP3 inflammasome formation, mitophagy impairment and mitochondrial apoptotic pathway activation. It discusses how the persistence of this inflammatory and dysfunctional state can lead to cardiac, muscular and neurological sequelae characterizing the post COVID-19 condition.
